# gitmoap_catalog_service (Resource)

Adds a service to the catalog, declared in this group and bound to one or more repository paths (an external service is not built here and binds none). Maintainers and above on the group may declare one; naming a group as owner needs the same standing on that group, naming a team needs authority over the team, and every bound repository must be one you maintain. The slug must be unique in the organization, and the number of services is capped by the plan.

The token needs `catalog:manage` and `catalog:read`.



<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `group_id` (String)
- `slug` (String)

### Optional

- `api_specs` (Attributes List) (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--api_specs))
- `description` (String)
- `display_name` (String) Defaults to the slug.
- `external` (Boolean) Whether the service is built outside gitmoap — a vendor SaaS, a service on another forge, a
database provisioned elsewhere. The catalog records its name, owner and the dependencies on
it, and nothing else. An external service has no repository paths.
- `kind` (String) What sort of thing a service is. The kind decides which scorecard checks apply: a `library` has
no deployments, so a deployment check is not applicable to it rather than failing. For your own
classifications, use annotations.
- `links` (Attributes List) (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--links))
- `owner_group_id` (String)
- `owner_principal_id` (String)
- `owner_team_id` (String)
- `provides` (Attributes List) (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--provides))
- `repo_paths` (Attributes List) (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--repo_paths))

### Read-Only

- `created_at` (String)
- `created_by` (Attributes) Who did something — a person, a service account or an AI organization's agent — with what a
client needs to draw and link them, so a page of records names its actors without a lookup each. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--created_by))
- `orphaned_at` (String) When the catalog file declaring this service stopped declaring it. The service is kept, with
its history, rather than deleted.
- `service_id` (String) The service's id
- `source` (String) How the catalog entry came to exist. Set by the platform, never accepted from a request. Any
source other than `inferred` means a person has vouched for the entry.
- `updated_at` (String)
- `version` (Number) The service's revision, incremented on every change. Send it with an update to have the
update refused with a `409` if someone changed the service since you read it.

<a id="nestedatt--api_specs"></a>
### Nested Schema for `api_specs`

Optional:

- `path` (String)
- `repository_id` (String)
- `spec_kind` (String) Which interface-description format a spec is written in.


<a id="nestedatt--links"></a>
### Nested Schema for `links`

Optional:

- `link_type` (String) What a service link points at. `other` covers anything the listed kinds do not.
- `url` (String)


<a id="nestedatt--provides"></a>
### Nested Schema for `provides`

Optional:

- `format` (String) The package ecosystem a registry speaks. A group has at most one registry per format.
- `name` (String)


<a id="nestedatt--repo_paths"></a>
### Nested Schema for `repo_paths`

Optional:

- `is_exclude` (Boolean) Whether this glob removes its matches from the service's paths instead of adding them. It
affects only its own service.
- `path_glob` (String)
- `repository_id` (String)

Read-Only:

- `path_prefix` (String) The longest literal prefix of `path_glob`, worked out by the platform. Read-only.


<a id="nestedatt--created_by"></a>
### Nested Schema for `created_by`

Read-Only:

- `avatar_url` (String) The principal's picture, when one is known. Absent otherwise: a client derives the
deterministic avatar URL itself.
- `email` (String) The principal's address. An agent's is a generated no-reply address — the author of its
commits. `unknown` on a deleted actor and empty on a redacted one.
- `id` (String) The principal's id: a user id, a service account id or an agent id, as `kind` says. Empty on
a redacted actor.
- `kind` (String) A person, a service account or an AI organization's agent — which of the three a principal is,
and so which page it links to: a person's profile, a service account's page or an agent's page.
- `username` (String) The name to show: a person's or service account's username, or an agent's handle (which
always ends in `-ai`). `deleted-user` when the actor no longer resolves, `redacted` when the
caller may not see who it was. A closed account whose work stays is `closed-` and twelve hex
digits, a shape no open account may take, with an address under `.invalid`.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Import by its group_id and service_id, joined with slashes.
terraform import gitmoap_catalog_service.example "<group_id>/<service_id>"
```
